mathematical_findings.finding: 07BJ gives equivalence of maximal-ideal inclusion and contraction for the inclusion A into B. Inclusion makes m_A B proper; conversely a proper ideal of local B lies in its unique maximal ideal by 00E0, forcing m_A into m_B. The contracted proper ideal contains maximal m_A and therefore equals it. Reflexivity, transitivity by successive contraction, and antisymmetry by the underlying inclusions are valid for local subrings of any common ring. The note correctly confines the cited 00I9 definition itself to field-subrings. No new theorem is necessary.

The localization universal map into K is injective: a/s maps to zero only when a=0, since s is nonzero in K. Specializing 00E3 to A minus p yields the unique maximal ideal p A_p and its contraction p, also explicitly discussed in the untagged locality paragraph. Embedded equality of two localizations therefore forces equality of their unique maximal ideals and hence their centers. Surjectivity is by the definition of L(A). The French indefinite wording does not assert that all local overrings occur; the note correctly excludes that false reading.

mathematical_findings.finding: The existence quantifier is correct: A contained in local M is equivalent to existence of some p with M dominating A_p. The unique p is m_M intersect A; elements of A minus p are units in M, so localization supplies the local inclusion. Necessity and uniqueness follow by contraction. Taking R=A, S=M, q=m_M in the actual untagged local-map paragraph gives the construction, using M_q=M. It is correct not to attribute that paragraph to the text of the tagged 07BI definition. Containment alone does not imply domination at a preselected p.

Unconditional L(A) intersect L(B) subset L(C): D=A_p=B_q contains C and dominates C_r for r=m_D intersect C. Conversely each denominator in A minus p lies in C minus r; hence A_p is contained in C_r and equality follows.

mathematical_findings.finding: All four quantified conditions and all proof steps are valid. In particular the step asserting D into C_r is local is justified by the previously read induced-local-map component, so the following invertibility argument is not circular. Spec(C) includes nonmaximal primes. Equality is literal inside the same K. The restriction in condition 1 to embedded local subrings of K correctly makes explicit the common-ambient convention used in the source proof; arbitrary incompatible maps out of A and B are not being admitted.

adversarial_examples.finding: Spec(Q) has only (0), so L(Q)={Q} inside Q(t), although Q[t]_(t) is a different local overring. This also tests the absence of an implicit K=Frac(A) assumption.
For A=Q[t] and M=Q[t]_(t), the ring A_(t-1) contains 1/t because t is not in (t-1), whereas M does not contain 1/t. Thus M contains A but not A_(t-1), and cannot dominate it.

Both Q[t]_(t) and Q[t]_(t-1) dominate Q, so each is allied to Q. In their generated ring the sum of the extended maximal ideals contains t and t-1, hence 1=t-(t-1). By 8.1.4 they are not allied to each other. The common field Q(t) is not a dominator of either nonfield local ring.

For A=Q[t], B=Q, C=A, every A_p contains t and therefore differs from Q. Thus L(A) intersect L(B) is empty while C_(0)=Q(t) lies in L(C). This correctly refutes automatic equality without challenging the unconditional opposite inclusion proved in the note.
